clues: This city lies on the coast in the southeast of Brazil, by the wide Atlantic shore. It forms part of a big metro zone round the state capital.
Winters here are dry and mild, while summers bring the rains. Cold fronts can sweep in at times and stir up strong gusts of wind.
A Portuguese man founded this town on 23 May 1535. He held the grant for the whole captaincy lands along this part of the coast.
Its big faith fest ranks as the third largest of its kind in Brazil. Crowds come each year to honor Our Lady with prayer and song.
High on a hill stands an old convent built in the 1500s and 1600s. It is a top sight and a prized piece of the past.
